messages:
maria: Heads up — since the rollout r2026-03-18-13 (merged yesterday) we're seeing a p95 jump (~+200ms) on SSE streaming in hosted. Spikes happen when requests include tool calls.

devon: Seen it on staging too. Repro: start a long stream, trigger a toolcall in the middle, the stream stalls for a bit. Profiling points to serialization / blocking on the worker thread.

aj: Can you paste the quick perf output or flame? Also did the merge touch kernel-autoselect, batching heuristics, or kv prefetch?

maria: Quick snippet from staging profiler: ```
# perf top -p <pid> (short)
40.1% protobuf::Serialize
12.3% memcpy
8.4% runtime.sched
6.7% eventloop pump
```
Full flame: https://gist.github.com/xyz/streaming-flame-2043 (short). Also saw GC bursts in node worker around the serialize spikes.

satoshi: FYI PR #1234 changed the streaming encode pipeline and bumped default batching_window from 5ms -> 30ms to reduce chattiness. Separately PR #1229 increased kv-prefetch concurrency from 2 -> 8. Both were merged in that rollout.

elaine: CI perf job flagged this earlier: perf-ci/streaming_p95 increased past threshold on 6f3a9c. @ci-bot posted the failure: https://ci.redwood/12345

ci-bot: Perf test fail on commit 6f3a9c — streaming_p95 120ms -> 138ms (threshold 10%).

devon: Suggest running a bisect: `git bisect start HEAD 6f3a9c^ && git bisect run ./tools/benchmark_streaming.sh` — will try a quick manual repro first.

maria: Quick config toggle: reverting batching_window to 5ms in staging brought p95 back near baseline. BUT when a toolcall is present, there's still ~60ms blocking in protobuf::Serialize. So seems like buffering change increased end-to-end impact but serialization is a separate hot path.

aj: That matches my suspicion: batching_window increase raises steady-state buffering latency; when combined with increased kv-prefetch concurrency it looks like CPU contention + sync serialization spikes the tail. We need to bisect which change makes serialization path hit harder.

satoshi: I ran a light bisect locally: revert PR 1234 (batching_window) recovers ~140ms of the regression; revert PR 1229 (kv-prefetch) recovers ~100ms. Together they compound to the full observed +200ms. Both touch unrelated subsystems but create a worse tail when combined.

ops: Rollout hold requested — please pause further rollouts for r2026-03-18-13. @deploy-bot hold this rollout.

deploy-bot: Rollout r2026-03-18-13 paused by ops. Notifying release owners.

maria: I'll open a revert PR for the batching_window change now (WIP). Also filing a follow-up to make proto serialization non-blocking for toolcall paths (switch to async streaming serialize or pre-serialized chunks).

aj: I'll add a synthetic integration to perf-suite that triggers a toolcall mid-stream so CI catches this class of regresses.

devon: I'll run a full bisect overnight to produce a clear blame commit range and test combined reverts.

satoshi: Also worth reviewing kernel-autoselect on encode kernels — if kernel choice shifts under higher concurrency we might be hitting a slower codepath for serializing small messages. I'll profile kernels next.

elaine: Action items summary: maria - revert PR #1234, aj - add perf integration, devon - full bisect, satoshi - kernel profiling, ops - release comms. Thanks everyone.

ci-bot: Re-run queued perf job for staging once revert PR is up.

maria: noted. Revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1250 — marking it as rollout-blocker.

ops: Received. Holding communications until we confirm perf recovery.
